record.context_brief: Three-colour vertex-Ramsey threshold for a 2-edge star
record.original_question: Determine the exact value of mcr(S_2,3), where S_2 is the 2-edge star and mcr(G,r) is the infimum of maximum average degrees of graphs that are vertex-Ramsey for G under r colours.

evidence.quote: Problem 5.8. Determine mcr(S2, 3) (no monetary award for that!)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_2$ denote the star with two edges, i.e., the graph on three vertices consisting of one central vertex adjacent to two leaves (equivalently, the path $P_3$). For a graph $G$ and a positive integer $r$, a graph $H$ is said to be vertex-Ramsey for $G$ with $r$ colours, written $H \to_v (G)_r$, if every $r$-colouring of the vertices of $H$ contains a monochromatic copy of $G$. The maximum average degree of a graph $H$ is
$$\mathrm{mad}(H) = \max_{\emptyset \neq H' \subseteq H} \frac{2|E(H')|}{|V(H')|}.$$
Define
$$\mathrm{mcr}(G, r) = \inf\bigl\{ \mathrm{mad}(H) : H \to_v (G)_r \bigr\}.$$
Determine the exact value of $\mathrm{mcr}(S_2, 3)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published determination of $\mathrm{mcr}(S_2,3)$. The problem is posed in an open-problem collection and no follow-up resolving the exact value was found, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Degree Ramsey numbers of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies degree-Ramsey style invariants for graphs including stars and trees, but does not give an exact value for mcr(S_2,3).
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on degree/average-degree Ramsey parameters for stars does not record a value for mcr(S_2,3).
